title: Night Ops: prefetch gambit & shadow cache check-in (week of 2027-11-01)
body:
Context:
Quick, slightly messy field notes from the late-night sync. Goal: consolidate what we actually tested during the prefetch + shadow cache spike, capture surprises, and lay out the minimal follow-ups for Monday. This is intentionally rough — notes-to-self + team crumbs.

When: 2027-11-02 23:00-00:30 PST (night-ops window)
Attendees (who touched infra): Aisha (lead), Marco (kernel), Liang (cache/metrics), Samantha (batching heuristics), Diego (deploy/ops)

Agenda
- Deploy kernel hotpatch v0.4.2 (small prefetch alignment change)
- Run shadow-cache experiment A (prefix-hash dedupe + TTL bump)
- Toggle microbatch interleaving with priority queue (alpha) on 20% of traffic
- Collect p50/p95/p99, KV hit-rate, memory pressure, and thermal events

High-level summary of outcomes
- Kernel hotpatch: harmless and beneficial for small prefix alignment workloads. p95 latency improved for short-seq (<=64) requests by ~8% (median p95 from 78ms -> 72ms). No regressions seen on long sequences.
- Shadow cache experiment A: KV hit-rate on the shadow path rose from baseline 6.8% -> 18.3% for the synthetic prompt set we used. However, memory churn increased on host nodes due to dedupe metadata (per-request bloom filter allocations) — need to reduce allocation frequency.
- Microbatch interleaving: cut end-to-end tail for mixed-priority streams in the canary slices by ~10-12ms, but observed a small increase in jitter for pure-high-priority lanes when bursty low-priority traffic arrived.
- No SLO breaches, but we saw two thermal throttle events during a 15-minute spike (machine-level sensor thresholds tripped) — Diego captured logs and evacuated a node.

Detailed notes by topic

1) Kernel hotpatch v0.4.2 (Marco)
- What changed: prefetch alignment window changed from fixed 8-token boundary to 2-token adaptive window when seq_len <= 64. Rationale: reduce wasted prefetch for many small completions.
- Observations: improved CPU scheduling fairness on our smaller CUDA contexts, reduced KV cache lock contention at the beginning of generation.
- Metrics: short-seq p50: 22ms -> 20ms, p95: 78ms -> 72ms, p99 unchanged within noise. Long-seq saw no measurable change.
- Risks: coupling to microbatching code path; if windows diverge we can get eviction/dup fetches. Marco: we should add a small compatibility test in runtime-integration that simulates mixed window sizes.
- Action: Marco to open INF-4925 to add the compatibility test + nightly job.

2) Shadow cache experiment A (Liang)
- Approach: build a parallel shadow cache layered above main KV that uses short-lived per-request prefix hashes to dedupe identical prefetch candidates. TTL bumped from 60s -> 120s for shadow entries so we can see reuse across quick retries.
- Good: increased apparent hit rate for our restarty prompt set and for multimodal infer where many initial prompts share prefixes.
- Bad: memory churn — we allocate small metadata structs (~48 bytes) per candidate; on heavy prefetch windows this added ~1.2GB on some nodes. Also observed an increase in GC-like pauses in our Python-side controller when the dedupe map hit thresholds.
- Workarounds tested: pooling metadata objects, switching to a compact bitset representation (reduced memory by ~3x in a tiny run).
- Decision: keep experiment A in shadow for now, but do not promote to production. Next step is to prototype memory-pooling and evaluate on a larger rig.
- Action: Liang to prototype object pool + compact-bitset and bench (INF-4899).

3) Batching + microbatch interleaving (Samantha)
- Alpha: priority-aware interleaving where small high-priority requests are allowed to jump ahead of buffered low-priority microbatches within the same kernel invocation window.
- Result: for mixed traffic (30% high-priority), overall p95 across high-priority dropped by 10-12ms. But there is a slight increase in variance for low-priority latencies (expected).
- Observed side effect: when low-priority bursts are sustained, kernel occupancy changes and we saw thermal effects on some GPUs (see below).
- Follow-up: refine admission control so high-priority gets guaranteed headroom but low-priority doesn't cause thermal escalation. Prototype: per-GPU energy-aware cap.
- Action: Samantha to write a short spec for energy-aware admission controls and microbatch weight decay (due 2027-11-08).

4) Thermal events and ops playbook (Diego)
- During the biggest synthetic spike we saw 2 thermal-throttle events across two machines in pool-6. Node evacuation worked as designed, but we should reduce the blast radius.
- Diego: logs captured, node replaced, incident doc skeleton opened (INF-4942).
- Short-term mitigation: add a tempering backoff in the microbatch scheduler when the node reports sustained high power draw for >30s.
- Action: Diego + Marco to add a probe into kernel scheduler to expose a soft-power metric via existing host telemetry (PR 1784 references).

5) Metrics & small dashboards (Liang)
- Quick numbers (canary slice, 2 hours):
  - Baseline KV hit-rate (no shadow): 6.8%
  - Shadow A apparent hit-rate: 18.3%
  - Short-seq p95 delta with kernel patch: -8%
  - Microbatch interleaving high-priority p95 delta: -11ms
  - Memory churn on nodes with shadow cache A: +1.0GB median
- Notes: these numbers are noisy; next run requires a longer window and more realistic traffic mix (we used heavy synthetic restarts).

Open questions / Unknowns
- How will shadow cache behave against real user traffic where prefixes are less synthetic? We might see lower reuse but still benefit for high-concurrency crowds.
- What is the simplest pool implementation that gives 3x memory reduction without adding latency?
- For kernel alignment windows, what happens when we have heterogenous model families on the same node? Need to simulate transformer variants.

Decisions made during the window
- Keep kernel hotpatch v0.4.2 in prod-canary for another 72h (no rollback unless we see p99 regressions).
- Mark shadow cache experiment A as lingering in shadow mode; do not promote. Prototype pooling before another canary.
- Microbatch interleaving stays at 20% canary, but enable tempering backoff guard to avoid thermal thrashing.

Action items (owners + rough ETA)
- INF-4925: kernel compatibility test (Marco) — ETA 2027-11-10
- INF-4899: shadow-cache memory pool prototype (Liang) — ETA 2027-11-09
- Spec: energy-aware admission control + microbatch weight decay (Samantha) — ETA 2027-11-08
- Infra probe: soft-power metric in kernel scheduler (Diego + Marco) — ETA 2027-11-12
- Incident doc skeleton: thermal-throttle postmortem (Diego) — ETA 2027-11-05

Personal notes / noise (Aisha)
- Notes to self: we need a better small-sequence workload generator that matches real product prompts. Synthetic restarty prompts are useful but bias decisions toward prefetch-heavy optimizations.
- Reminder: ping legal/infra about any memory pooling using jemalloc hooks — potential rebuild cost.
- Thought: could we offload dedupe metadata into a tiny LRU on-disk segment for very low-cost dedupe sinces it's mostly for short-lived prefixes? Probably overkill but jotting it down.

Next sync (quick)
- Monday 2027-11-08 09:30 PST — status on INF-4899 + INF-4925, and review of extended metric window for shadow A (want 12h of real-prod-like traffic).

Appendix (quick links we referenced)
- Kernel PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1784
- Shadow experiment branch: github.com/redwood-inference/cache-experiments/tree/shadow-a
- JIRA: INF-4821 (prefetch cleanup), INF-4899 (shadow cache), INF-4925 (compat-tests), INF-4942 (thermal incident)

End of scribbles. If anything here seems off or you want a different breakdown (more graphs or exported csv), shout and I'll attach the raw metrics dump.
summary: Late-night field notes: kernel hotpatch shows small p95 wins for short sequences, shadow cache increases apparent KV hit rates but caused memory churn, microbatch interleaving improves high-priority tail but can induce thermal issues. Actions assigned for pooling, compat tests, and energy-aware admission control.
